basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 11.' and it opens 'VERS. 11.-- Dixitque Jacob ad Dominum: Erue me de manu fratris mei Esau, quia valde eum'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 11.-- Dixitque Jacob ad Dominum: Erue me de manu fratris mei Esau, quia valde eum timeo. Quaeri solet quomodo fidem habuerit Jacob, quandoquidem tantum timuit Esau fratrem suum? Satis enim in verbis ejusdem Jacob, quae sequuntur, et humana infirmitas et fides pietatis apparet; ut et Deus liberaret eum, et quae promisit impleret. Admonendi tamen fuimus hoc exemplo ut, quamvis credamus in Deum, faciamus tamen quae facienda sunt | ab hominibus in praesidium salutis, ne praetermittentes ea, Deum tentare videamur.
